name: net_desync_dump_keeps_level
description: The desync dump carries the level (M8, contract-m8 §3: format 2, a u8 level after the mode). A High Water dev match at Very Hard, two seats played by the plan bots; a bug writes client 2's gold past tick 2,000, the two seats part and the match ends desynced. Each dump is format 2 and names level 2 (Very Hard); replayed from its checkpoint at that level, client 2's turns reach client 1's hash. A dump written by a format-1 game (no level byte) still reads, as Normal; one whose level byte names no level reads as no dump, and replay takes no level outside the wire's, so a corrupt dump never replays at the wrong level.

steps.msg: two seats apart: desynced, a dump each

steps.assert: d1['format'] == 2 and d2['format'] == 2 and d1['difficulty'] == 2 and d2['difficulty'] == 2 and d1['mode'] == 1
steps.msg: format 2 names the level after the mode: Very Hard (2) in High Water
client 2's dump replays at its level to client 1's hash

steps.assert: old['format'] == 1 and old['difficulty'] == 0 and old['mode'] == 1 and old['seed'] == 11 and old['bad_tick'] == bad and old['hashes'] == d1['hashes']
steps.msg: a format-1 dump still reads, its level Normal

steps.assert: hard['format'] == 2 and hard['difficulty'] == 1 and hard['bad_tick'] == bad
steps.msg: the level byte sits where LEVEL_AT says: a dump rewritten to name Hard reads as Hard
a dump whose level byte names no level is no dump: read refuses it rather than replay it at Normal
and replay takes no level outside the wire's
